neighbours.label: Fires on the question mark and closing quote ending a spoken question in fiction dialogue ('"What?" he said'); quiet on quoted statements and on questions in expository or reported form.
fire: Mara looked up from her book. "Who's there?" she called.
"I sold the house," he said. "You what?" she gasped.
The boy tugged at his father's sleeve. "Are we nearly home?"
"Did you hear that?" Tom whispered, gripping the rail.
She frowned at the letter. "Why would he write this?"
Lucy pointed at herself. "Why me?" she asked.
"Where were you last night?" his mother demanded.
The guard stepped forward. "What do you want?"
quiet: Mara looked up from her book. "Come in," she called.
"I sold the house," he said. "Good," she replied.
The boy tugged at his father's sleeve and pointed toward home.
Tom whispered that he had heard something, gripping the rail.
She frowned at the letter and wondered why he had written it.
Why do some birds migrate at night? Scientists think it helps them avoid predators.
Where were the ancient Olympics held? They took place at Olympia.
The guard stepped forward and asked what the visitor wanted.

predictions: median fire ~0.35 (probes: '"What?"' 0.74, '"Whatever do you mean?"' 0.39; echo '"Help me?"' only 0.08); near misses < 0.1 (quoted statement 0.05, expository question 0.005); risk: quoted reply 'Yes, ... tell me.' 0.26.
